For animation evidence, Python also receives `frame_sequence`, `last_action_frames`, and `animation_frames`; inspect any frame with `frame_sequence.at(i)` or summarize all of them with `frame_sequence.summaries()` and `frame_sequence.diff(...)`.
Only letter-coded board views and lightweight metadata are exposed; raw numeric color IDs are not available.
Keep tool output compact: use `current_frame.segmentation` as the primary view, and `current_frame.ascii` only for a small specific region; never print full boards.
For the most recent change, compare `previous_frame` to `current_frame`, or `last_transition.before_frame` to `last_transition.after_frame`; `history[-1].frame` is the current frame, not the previous one.
Use Python to inspect the evidence, refine that world model from the newest history, and search or score candidate actions or short sequences against the current goal as you currently understand it.
Maintain a compact working world model of what the current level seems to contain, what actions appear to do, what the goal seems to be, what is still uncertain, and what plan currently looks best.

You may call `action(actions)` more than once in one Python snippet if your search or control loop needs it, but stop immediately if a result reports `game_over`, `run_complete`, `level_completed`, or `done`.
Working world model carried from earlier turns:
- World model: ** the beam is a hazard when the player occupies cols 36-39 at fire time (possibly only near the bottom). I need a controlled test: put the player in the beam path at a *safe* height and fire. - Goal still unknown; arches (yellow, cols 16-27 & 40-51) and the top emitter are the only special objects.
- Recent findings: - Full run reconstruction: start (16,19,12,31) → several safe beam fires at mid heights → moved down to (44,47,36,55) → SPACE → GAME OVER → RESET to start. - The "activate the arch" hypothesis was wrong; the arches are hazards. The beam scan at safe heights is a no-op (reverts), so the real goal mechanic is still unknown, but the bottom is a death zone. Open questions (for a future/restarted run only): - What is the actual win condition? The mid-height beam scans reverted with no visible effect, so the objective is not simply "scan the arches." Likely the beam must be fired at a specific target/height, or the arches must be avoided entirely. - Whether GAME_OVER here is a hard terminal or a retry — the auto-RESET to start is ambiguous, but `stop_reason: game_over` + reward 0.0 indicates a lost run.
- Plan: - Controlled experiment: move RIGHT twice (player → cols 20-39, so its right edge enters the beam path) at the safe start height (rows 16-19), then fire SPACE. If game-over → beam is a height-independent hazard; if safe → the death was bottom-proximity specific.
- Cross-level notes: - Movement granularity is 4 cells; the board is effectively a 16×16 logical grid (64/4). Track the player by the blue 4×20 block's bounding box. Never fire SPACE when the player's bottom edge is within a few rows of the yellow arches. I will not call `action(...)` this turn because the run has ended in game-over.
- Revise any item above immediately if `current_frame` or `history` contradicts it.
end of world model.

If you include assistant text before a tool call, keep it short and use it to update the world model. Helpful optional prefixes are `World model:`, `Goal model:`, `Action model:`, `Recent findings:`, `Open questions:`, `Plan:`, and `Cross-level notes:`.
When calling `python`, emit exactly the tool-call format shown elsewhere in this prompt for this model. Use only that format; do not add markdown fences, prose wrappers, or alternate tool-call syntax. Do not quote or place tool-call markup inside explanatory text; when you decide to call the tool, emit the tool call itself.
If you use MOUSE, include integer row and col arguments.
